# Brief — Feature Flag & Canary Rollout Controller

## Problem
Percentage rollouts that call `Math.random()` reshuffle users on every request, and canaries that only page a human still ship a bad build to the rest of the cohort.

## Target users
Backend and frontend owners running a progressive rollout.

## Core behavior
- Bucket `fnv1a(flag + ':' + subject) % 100`. A subject is enrolled when `bucket < percentage`.
- Record canary outcomes. When samples reach `minSamples` and `errors / samples >= errorThreshold`, set `rolledBack` and force the percentage to 0.

## Files
- `domain.js` — hash, controller, circuit breaker.
- `app.js` — isomorphic facade.
- `test.js` — deterministic hash, enrollment, and rollback assertions.
- `index.html` — dark-mode rollout simulator.

# Runbook — Feature Flag & Canary Rollout Controller

## Contract
- `fnv1a(text)` returns an unsigned 32-bit FNV-1a hash.
- `defineFlag({ key, percentage, errorThreshold, minSamples })` clamps percentage to 0..100.
- `bucket(key, subjectId)` is pure for a given flag state. Percentage `0` enrolls nobody. Percentage `100` enrolls every bucket `0..99`.
- `recordOutcome(key, { error })` increments samples and, when the rate crosses the threshold, rolls the flag back.
- Rollback uses `>=`, so a rate that lands exactly on the threshold trips.

## Do not
- Do not invert the circuit comparison.
- Do not use `Math.random` for enrollment.
- Do not add npm dependencies.

# Brief — Feature Flag & Canary Rollout Controller

## Problem
Percentage rollouts that call `Math.random()` reshuffle users on every request, and canaries that only page a human still ship a bad build to the rest of the cohort.

## Target users
Backend and frontend owners running a progressive rollout.

## Core behavior
- Bucket `fnv1a(flag + ':' + subject) % 100`. A subject is enrolled when `bucket < percentage`.
- Record canary outcomes. When samples reach `minSamples` and `errors / samples >= errorThreshold`, set `rolledBack` and force the percentage to 0.

## Files
- `domain.js` — hash, controller, circuit breaker.
- `app.js` — isomorphic facade.
- `test.js` — deterministic hash, enrollment, and rollback assertions.
- `index.html` — dark-mode rollout simulator.

# Runbook — Feature Flag & Canary Rollout Controller

## Contract
- `fnv1a(text)` returns an unsigned 32-bit FNV-1a hash.
- `defineFlag({ key, percentage, errorThreshold, minSamples })` clamps percentage to 0..100.
- `bucket(key, subjectId)` is pure for a given flag state. Percentage `0` enrolls nobody. Percentage `100` enrolls every bucket `0..99`.
- `recordOutcome(key, { error })` increments samples and, when the rate crosses the threshold, rolls the flag back.
- Rollback uses `>=`, so a rate that lands exactly on the threshold trips.

## Do not
- Do not invert the circuit comparison.
- Do not use `Math.random` for enrollment.
- Do not add npm dependencies.

## 1. Problem
Modern teams ship features progressively but lack safe, deterministic rollout control. Random percentage rollouts cause inconsistent UX (user flickers in/out), canary errors go undetected until blast radius grows, and manual rollback is slow. There is no zero-dependency, browser-runnable controller that guarantees sticky bucketing, detects canary degradation via error-rate circuit breaker, and auto-rolls back.

## 2. Target Users
- **Engineers** doing progressive delivery who need deterministic per-user targeting
- **SREs / Release Managers** monitoring canary health and needing automatic safety nets
- **Product Managers** controlling exposure % without backend complexity

## 3. Core Features

### A. Deterministic FNV-1a Percentage Bucketing
- Pure JS FNV-1a 32-bit: OFFSET `2166136261`, PRIME `16777619`, with `>>>0` overflow
- `bucket = fnv1a(userId + ':' + flagKey) % 100` → 0-99
- `isInRollout = bucket < percentage`; 0% = none, 100% = all; sticky per user+flag
- No randomness; same user+flag always same bucket

### B. Progressive Rollout Controller
- Flag lifecycle: `disabled` (0%), `canary` (1-10%), `progressive` (11-99%), `enabled` (100%), `rolled_back`
- CRUD flags: `key, name, description, percentage (0-100), threshold (0-100), status, lastStablePercentage, createdAt, updatedAt`
- Slider + step controls (+1%, +5%, +10%, +25%) with audit log
- Evaluation API: `evaluateFlag(flagKey, userId)` returns `{enabled, bucket, reason, percentage}`

### C. Canary Error-Rate Circuit Breaker
- Per-flag metrics: `totalRequests, errorCount, errorRate = errors/total`
- Configurable threshold (default 5%) and `minSample` (default 20 requests)
- `checkCircuitBreaker()` trips if `errorRate > threshold && total >= minSample && status !== 'disabled'`
- Visual status: `CLOSED` (healthy) / `OPEN` (tripped)

### D. Auto-Rollback
- On breaker `OPEN`: auto-rollback to `lastStablePercentage` (or 0%), set `status='rolled_back'`, freeze rollout, log event with timestamp/reason
- Manual resume/retry after investigation
- Audit log tracks all transitions: create, update, percentage change, breaker trip, rollback

### E. UI & Persistence
- Dark-mode dashboard: flag table, create/edit modal, evaluator playground, metrics + breaker panel, audit timeline
- `localStorage` persistence + in-memory fallback; zero backend

## 4. Architecture
- **Zero-dependency, single `app.js` dual-mode module** (CommonJS for Node + `window.FlagController` for browser)
- Pure functions for hashing/breaker; stateful store for flags/metrics/audit
- `index.html` is view layer only, calls `app.js` APIs; no business logic in HTML
- `test.js` runs in Node via `require('./app.js')` asserting determinism, breaker, rollback
- Self-contained, immediately runnable, no build step, no fetch, no npm install

- `fnv1a(str: string): number` — 32-bit unsigned FNV-1a, returns `>>>0`

- `Flag = { key, name, description, percentage:0-100, threshold:0-100, status, lastStablePercentage, createdAt, updatedAt }`

- `evaluateFlag(flagKey, userId, attributes?): { enabled:boolean, bucket:number, reason:string, percentage:number }` — returns disabled if flag missing/disabled, else bucket check

# Runbook — Feature Flag & Canary Rollout Controller

## Contract
- `fnv1a(text)` returns an unsigned 32-bit FNV-1a hash.
- `defineFlag({ key, percentage, errorThreshold, minSamples })` clamps percentage to 0..100.
- `bucket(key, subjectId)` is pure for a given flag state. Percentage `0` enrolls nobody. Percentage `100` enrolls every bucket `0..99`.
- `recordOutcome(key, { error })` increments samples and, when the rate crosses the threshold, rolls the flag back.
- Rollback uses `>=`, so a rate that lands exactly on the threshold trips.

## Do not
- Do not invert the circuit comparison.
- Do not use `Math.random` for enrollment.
- Do not add npm dependencies.
